parts.label: c
parts.display_text: A missile is launched from a rocket moving at +0.80c relative to Earth. Its velocity relative to the rocket is −0.62c. Calculate the velocity of the missile relative to Earth. (The source mistakenly asks for the rocket velocity.)

source.collection_label: International Baccalaureate · 2016 official HL and SL specimen pack with mark schemes
source.title: 2016 official HL and SL specimen pack with mark schemes

sup-59a633a1a2b93971-q10:whole.hint: Start from the definition of γ and rearrange for v/c before substituting.
notes: γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²), so squaring and rearranging isolates the dimensionless speed ratio.
γ is at least one for a material inertial observer. Check that the resulting speed is below c and has the correct units.

sup-5e62e7fd42677f6d-q9:whole.hint: Identify the frame in which the two events happen at the same place. Its clock measures the proper time.
notes: Time dilation is Δt = γΔτ, with γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²). Proper time is measured by one clock present at both events.
Use distances and speeds measured in the same frame. If a journey time is L/v in the Earth frame, the travelling clock records that interval divided by γ.

sup-5e62e7fd42677f6d-q10:whole.hint: Write down the position and time of each event in the frame where they are given before transforming them.
notes: For S′ moving at +v relative to S, x′ = γ(x − vt) and t′ = γ(t − vx/c²). Use the inverse transformation, with +v, to go from S′ to S.
Simultaneity depends on the frame for spatially separated events. On a spacetime diagram, check whether the time axis is t or ct before reading slopes.

sup-b58813f37227cecc-q10:whole.hint: At speeds comparable with c, ordinary addition of velocities is no longer valid.
notes: For collinear motion, u′ = (u − v)/(1 − uv/c²), with signed velocities. Use the inverse relation for the opposite transformation.
Check the low-speed limit and that a light signal still has speed c. A result exceeding c for a material object indicates a sign or formula error.

sup-1aff23cca0941015-q1:whole.hint: At speeds comparable with c, ordinary addition of velocities is no longer valid.

sup-1aff23cca0941015-q2:whole.hint: Draw the velocities with their reference frames labelled. Which two vectors combine to give the required motion?
notes: At non-relativistic speeds, v(A relative to C) = v(A relative to B) + v(B relative to C). Resolve perpendicular directions separately.
For a magnitude and direction, combine the components using Pythagoras and a labelled angle. Do not add the magnitudes of perpendicular velocities.
